correctness.rationale: PASS. The transformation that deletes the first one and appends it, applied k times, maps the ith zero position z_i to max(i,z_i−k), including k beyond the word’s number of ones. This preserves prefix-zero dominance and therefore monotone lexicographic phase ordering for lower-mechanical Sturmian coding. There are n+1 distinct phase factor intervals cut by fractional parts {−jα}, j=0..n. The final-letter boundary x_n cannot merge because one-count changes. For j=1..n−1, adjacent words are p01s/p10s; they have the same k-step output precisely when prefix p contains fewer than k ones. Its one count is ceil(jα)−1, so exactly min(n−1,floor(k/α)) boundaries merge for irrational α. Thus rho_(α,k)(n)=max(2,n+1−floor(k/α)) for all n≥1,k≥2, and n=0 gives 1. The agreement cutoff floor(k/α)+1 and slope limit k/floor(k/α)→α follow. Independent high-precision irrational mechanical-factor simulation checked 154 (n,k) cases (n=1..22,k=1..7) and reproduced the formula; finite simulation is corroboration only.
